body.statement: There is a deterministic algorithm that, after \(2^{O(b\log b)}\operatorname{poly}(|V|+|E^{\mathrm{det}}|+|E^{?}|)\) preprocessing, enumerates every member of \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) exactly once with the same worst-case delay and polynomial working space; its first output and exhaustion obey the same bound, every output is globally minimal, and each output receives a canonical original-query ID failure label.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel converting one uncertain causal graph into a complete, auditable antichain of failure explanations.
body.gap: The nearest causal algorithms return one optimal edge deletion or discover only the hedges needed for an intervention optimum; no cited result proves output-sensitive uncertain-edge support enumeration.
body.consumer: The uncertain-ADMG sampler and edgeID workflow can report every minimal jointly harmful edge combination rather than one selected identifiable realization.

obligation.what_is_open: The general-\(b\) construction of a polynomial-size root-ordered partial-support state, an on-demand child iterator, and a nonempty-completion test with \(2^{O(b\log b)}\operatorname{poly}(|V|+|E^{\mathrm{det}}|+|E^{?}|)\) worst-case cost, together with a canonical cross-core owner that removes equality duplicates and strict domination before a leaf is reached.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen dependency \texttt{oeq:canonical-partial-support-recursion} is still an unanswered sibling-owned question, not an established premise.  The supplied draft proves only a private-root dominator-chain condition for completed relative-minimal supports; it explicitly does not prove that this condition is stable under partial extension or sufficient for a completion oracle.  A finite state alone also does not imply the target's polynomial-space claim: its encoding and iterator records must have polynomial size, cores must be generated on demand, and duplicate suppression cannot store all prior outputs.  These are precisely the novel kernel, so assuming them or narrowing to the already-solved \(b\le 2\) class would not prove the stated theorem.
obligation.attempted: Extended the established sparse-core reduction by analyzing depth-first traversal costs and isolated five sufficient search-forest invariants.  Per-core minimal directed-support enumeration followed by global filtering fails to bound gaps, because exponentially many projected witnesses or candidates owned by other cores may occur between new outputs.  The completed-support private-root assignment does not define stable children for partial supports.  Deterministic projection solves the single-root \(b\le 2\) case, while the supplied draft records no construction extending it to shared multi-root paths and competing cores.
obligation.partial_result:
Put
\[
 n=|V|+|E^{\mathrm{det}}|+|E^{?}|,
 \qquad m=|E^{?}|.
\]
The established sparse-core reduction gives at most
\(M=|V|2^{O(b\log(b+1))}\) core templates and identifies
\(\mathcal O_{XY}\) with the globally inclusion-minimal members of their
root-to-outcome support families.  The remaining implication can be made
precise as follows.  Suppose the sibling open question is resolved by a
canonical search forest having: (i) depth at most \(m+1\); (ii) states and
iterator records of size \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\); (iii) an on-demand
root iterator and next-live-child operation taking
\(\Delta=2^{O(b\log(b+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n)\) time and polynomial
space; (iv) at least one leaf below every live child; and (v) a bijection
between its leaves and \(\mathcal O_{XY}\), implemented by a canonical
cross-core owner so that neither equality duplicates nor strictly dominated
supports become leaves.  A depth-first traversal then reaches its first leaf
after at most \(m+1\) live transitions once a live root is found.  Between
two consecutive leaves it ascends at most \(m+1\) levels, advances one root
or child iterator, and descends at most \(m+1\) levels.  Scanning all
\(M\) possible roots when necessary costs at most
\(M\Delta=2^{O(b\log(b+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n)\).  Hence preprocessing,
delay, and the post-last-output exhaustion test all have that bound.  The
stack contains at most \(m+1\) polynomial-size records, while the core
iterator is generated on demand and no emitted-support table is stored, so
working space is polynomial in \(n\).  Property (v) and the sparse-core
reduction give coverage, global minimality, and exact-once output.  Finally,
running the fixed deterministic ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\) procedure
on each emitted realization supplies its canonical original-query failure
label at polynomial additional cost.  Thus every conclusion of the target
theorem follows from the displayed five search-forest properties; what is
not proved is the existence of a forest satisfying (ii)--(v) for general
\(b\).
